name: Downtown and the Public Plaza
tagline: The old centre around the plaza and San Sebastian Cathedral
description: Bacolod's historic core around the public plaza, the cathedral and the old provincial capitol with its lagoon. The public market, the jeepney terminals and Manokan Country, the row of chicken inasal grills, are all here. It is the busiest and cheapest part of the city.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the market, the plaza and the inasal grills on foot
pros: Manokan Country and the public market close by
The lowest rents in the city
cons: Congested and noisy through the day

name: Mandalagan and the Reclamation Area
tagline: The newer commercial strip, malls and condominiums
description: The northern commercial belt along Lacson Street and out to the reclamation area, where the malls, the newer condominium towers, the restaurants and the coffee shops have concentrated over the last fifteen years. It is where most foreigners end up and where the internet is best.
bestFor: Stays wanting a modern condo, reliable fibre and the restaurants nearby
pros: Newest apartments and the most reliable connections
Where the city's social scene has moved
cons: Traffic on Lacson Street at peak times

name: Villamonte and Capitol Area
tagline: Residential streets around the capitol lagoon
description: The established residential district behind the capitol, with older houses, tree-lined streets, small businesses and a settled middle-class character. It sits between the downtown and the newer northern strip, which makes it walkable to both and quieter than either.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a quiet street within reach of both centres
pros: Walking distance to both downtown and Lacson
cons: Some streets flood in heavy rain

name: Talisay and the Northern Suburbs
tagline: Out past The Ruins, with space and lower rents
description: The suburban belt running north into Talisay City, where the sugar-baron mansions once stood and where The Ruins, the burnt shell of an Italianate house, now sits among the cane fields. Housing here is subdivisions and houses with gardens at rents well below the city.
bestFor: Long stays wanting a house and a garden, with a ride into the city
pros: Houses with gardens at low rents
The Ruins and the cane country nearby
Quieter and cooler than the city
cons: Twenty to thirty minutes into Bacolod
A vehicle or regular jeepney rides are necessary

name: Silay Heritage District (20 km north)
tagline: The preserved sugar-era town near the airport
description: A separate small city twenty kilometres north, holding the best surviving concentration of Philippine sugar-boom mansions, several of them open as museums, along with a quiet old quarter. Bacolod's airport is here, and the road into the city takes about thirty minutes.
bestFor: Stays that want the heritage houses and the airport rather than the city
pros: The best preserved heritage architecture in the region
Quiet small-town pace and low rents
